# DOHaD India Regional Society
> Developmental Origins of Health and Disease (DOHaD) India Regional Society advances research, capacity building, clinical translation, and health policy regarding early life development, maternal-fetal nutrition, epigenetics, and adult non-communicable disease (NCD) etiology in the Indian and South Asian context.

## About the Organization
- **Official Name**: DOHaD India Regional Society (DOHaD India)
- **Affiliation**: Regional chapter of the International DOHaD Society (https://dohadsociety.org)
- **Primary Website**: https://www.dohadindia.org
- **Contact**: contact@dohadindia.org
- **Geographic Focus**: India & South Asia

## Core Research & Action Pillars
1. **Biological & Epigenetic Mechanisms**: Investigating how developmental exposures (e.g., maternal undernutrition, gestational diabetes, environmental toxins, micronutrient deficiencies) induce structural, metabolic, and epigenetic changes that predispose individuals to cardiovascular diseases, type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and obesity.
2. **Clinical & Community Translation**: Translating developmental biology findings into maternal, infant, and adolescent health interventions across healthcare settings in India.
3. **Capacity Building & Training**: Conducting regional workshops, methodology masterclasses, early-career investigator mentorship, and academic conferences.
4. **Policy & Advocacy**: Working with Indian governmental bodies (e.g., ICMR, MoHFW, NITI Aayog), academic medical institutions, and global health partners to embed life-course health priorities into national public health policy.
